summary: Design tuner puts a live preview next to a few sliders, such as radius, padding, spacing and shadow, so a person can tweak a component by hand. A button hands the same sliders to the agent, which can move them while people watch and then explain what it changed.
use: When people and the agent should share control over a component's look.
When you want the agent's styling choices to be visible as slider moves, not hidden in code.
When designers want to fine-tune spacing or radius after the agent has made a first pass.
When you need a short note from the agent about why it picked the new values.
features: Each entry in `params` becomes a slider with a label, a range, a unit like px, and optional `decimals` for fine values.
Every value is set on the preview as a CSS variable named `--dm-<key>`, so your styles can read it.
`preview` lets you render your own component. It receives the values and a style object with those variables. Without it, a sample pricing card is shown.
`active` highlights the slider the agent is moving, and `status` shows a short line like "Agent is tuning".
The tune button calls `onTune`. While `tuning` is true it shows a thinking animation and ignores clicks.
`note` shows the agent's explanation above the button, and `actionLabel` lets you change it to something like "Tune again".
a11y: Each slider has `role="slider"`, is focusable, and sets `aria-label`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow` and `aria-valuetext`.
Arrow keys move a slider by one step, or by the smallest decimal when `decimals` is set.
The tune button sets `aria-busy` while the agent is tuning.

faq.q: How do I let the agent move the sliders?
faq.a: Control `values` and update them from your agent as it works. Set `tuning` and `active` while it runs so people can see which slider it is on.

faq.q: How do I tune my own component instead of the sample card?
faq.a: Pass `preview`, a function that gets the values and a style object. Spread the style onto your element and read the `--dm-<key>` variables in its CSS.

faq.q: Can a slider hold decimal values?
faq.a: Yes. Set `decimals` on the param, for example 2 for a shadow strength. The value is shown and set with that many decimals instead of being rounded.
